data.hypothesis: Horner-only evaluation measured 0.007254 s, faster than the 0.007529 s baseline; sqrtf(T) sharing alone and combined with Horner measured 0.008214 s and 0.008066 s, respectively. The earlier balanced partial-sum rewrite measured 0.007276 s. This contrasting even/odd factorization computes k² and k⁴, then evaluates independent polynomial groups; it may shorten the dependency chain, but its extra arithmetic and changed float evaluation order may instead hurt time or rounding. sqrtf expressions remain unchanged for an isolated test.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these results to motivate a distinct polynomial grouping test, while requiring fresh correctness and timing measurements before retaining it.
memory_lessons.claim: In the available T3 measurements, Horner-only evaluation was valid at 0.007254 s, faster than the 0.007529 s baseline. Sharing sqrtf(T) alone measured 0.008214 s and Horner plus sharing measured 0.008066 s. A balanced partial-sum variant measured 0.007276 s. These are measured outcomes, not proof of why the variants differed.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the even/odd factorization on varied inputs and compare its correctness and time with the existing Horner and balanced-group candidates.

data.notes: The catalog reports four valid, distinct T3 programs and no duplicates. This candidate changes only the CND polynomial evaluation: the even/odd factorization preserves all supplied coefficients and the surrounding formula, while changing float operation order. sqrtf(T), the Black-Scholes expressions, binomial code, and entrypoint are unchanged. Correctness across varied inputs and performance remain for the controller to evaluate; no speedup is assumed.
